solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sound of air that's nothing quiet?

parts.note: that, as a relative pronoun, can be replaced by who; the apostrophe-s adds no letters
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether the sound of moving air is really just silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The rush of air past something fast makes exactly this onomatopoeic noise.

clue.text: Laundry room item was focal point around start of twenties

indicators.note: the hub word wraps around the following letter, so it is a container signal

parts.note: a hub is the central point of activity

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the word twenties

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a laundry fixture was the centre of the home back in the twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts T, the opening letter of 'twenties', within the focal point; the surface's decade points to the era of the household wash day.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub for washing clothes is a fixture of a laundry room.

clue.text: Pale 5

definitions.meaning: looking pale means looking unwell, slightly ill
the answer to 5 down is blue, meaning risqué or smutty

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly ill shows in a pallid face; a joke in poor taste is also described this way, just like a blue joke.

clue.text: One into guitar's sound

indicators.note: into says the numeral goes inside the guitar name

parts.note: the Strat, short for Stratocaster, is a famous electric guitar; the 's is no letter
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is getting into the tone a guitar makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of sea joining two larger bodies of water, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Hairstyle a setter's kept short? Anything but

indicators.note: kept says the hairstyle is held inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short says the setter's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Dante is the pseudonym of a long-serving Financial Times crossword setter; setter's here means setter has
a bun is hair gathered into a knot

explanation.surface: A question about whether a setter wears a hairstyle short, answered with an emphatic no.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante is a long-time FT setter's pen name; 'short' drops its last letter. The definition 'Anything but' leans on 'short': the opposite of short in quantity is plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything but short means plentiful, in generous supply.

clue.text: Unsuitable for young Conservative

definitions.meaning: risqué or smutty material is not suitable for children
the colour of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.definitionFit: Blue means indecent, like a blue film, and is also the party colour of British Tories.

clue.text: Drug investigator is beginning to sniff one's plants

parts.note: a narc is US slang for a narcotics agent
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word sniff

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A narcotics officer sniffs a suspect's plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi, daffodils and their relatives, are flowering bulb plants.

clue.text: A little love is not primarily without unexpected cost

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the five words that come before it

explanation.surface: A romantic insists that love comes with no hidden costs.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-in price includes every charge, so nothing extra turns up later.

clue.text: Engineers have dug earth around plant

indicators.note: around says the teat and earth pieces wrap round the engineers

parts.note: a dug is an udder or teat of an animal
E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers have dug the soil around a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' looks like a past tense verb but is a noun, an animal's teat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea tree is an Australasian shrub whose oil is widely used.

clue.text: Trip through Africa's wild (avoiding Cape)

indicators.note: wild says the remaining letters run riot into a new order
avoiding says the cape letter is left out

parts.note: the word Africa's supplies its letters, the S included
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A trip across untamed Africa that skips the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes C from AFRICAS, leaving AFRIAS; 'wild' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition or journey, especially one to view wildlife.

clue.text: I'll argue about alternative spelling for "irregular"

definitions.note: irregular as a noun means an irregular soldier; the answer's usual spelling has a double R

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pedant argues over another way of spelling a word for an irregular fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerrillas are irregular fighters, and this single-R form is an accepted variant spelling.

clue.text: It has much farmland and not people

parts.note: nor means and not
folk means people

explanation.surface: A place with plenty of fields but no inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: NORFOLK is a largely agricultural county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This East Anglian county is famous for its flat arable land and farming.

clue.text: Room isn't arranged as groups of three cells

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A room that has not been arranged into a three-cell layout.
explanation.definitionFit: In recreational maths, polyomino shapes made of three joined squares are named this way.

clue.text: Drawn towards private serving in 20?

definitions.note: 20 across is a mess, a military dining hall, where meals are served

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for drawn in sports results tables
inner means private, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: Someone feels drawn towards a private matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The main evening meal is a serving of food, such as one eaten in an officers' mess.

clue.text: Panic about Euro beat

indicators.note: about says the panic word goes around the euro letter

parts.note: being in a lather means agitated, panicking

explanation.surface: Alarm about the beaten-down euro.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather someone is to thrash them, as with a belt.

clue.text: I hope you're scared by knight's tale

parts.note: boo is what you shout to frighten someone
K is the abbreviation for knight, as in KBE; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by a knight's spooky story.
explanation.definitionFit: A book is a written story, so it can stand for a tale.

clue.text: A smelly sweet to eat

definitions.note: a smelly is used as a noun here: something that smells

parts.note: afters is British for dessert, the sweet course
to have a meal means to eat it

explanation.surface: A pungent dessert someone is supposed to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is the informal British name for a pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented lotion applied to the face after a wet razor counts as a perfumed product.

clue.text: Stunned bridge player surrounded by a mob

indicators.note: surrounded by says the bridge player sits inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
a ruck is a crowd or mob
West is one of the four seats in bridge

explanation.surface: A card player is dazed after being encircled by a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overcome with wonder is to be stunned into silence.

clue.text: In Ireland my drinks will contain punch

definitions.note: my is an exclamation of surprise; the def is an Irish form of it

indicators.note: will contain says the drinks wrap around the punch

parts.note: beers are drinks
a jab is a quick punch

explanation.surface: An Irishman warns that his drinks will have some punch.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish oath of surprise, a mild version of by Jesus, used like my goodness.

clue.text: Material for trapping Romeo in school, the pervert!

indicators.note: trapping says the scrambled letters close around the phonetic letter
pervert as a verb means to twist, so the letters of school and the are distorted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for evidence to trap a corrupt teacher at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pervert' looks like a noun of abuse but is the anagram signal: SCHOOLTHE becomes HOSECLOTH, and 'trapping' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth covering for a horse is a fabric, part of its trappings.

clue.text: Witch drinks cold blood which causes coughing

indicators.note: drinks says the witch takes in the other letters

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
blood means kin, family

explanation.surface: A witch drinking chilly blood ends up with a cough.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, dry, repeated cough is described with this word.

clue.text: Some of this becomes strawberry jam

definitions.meaning: Eton ... is a pudding of strawberries, cream and meringue
jam means a predicament or muddle

explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam is being in a muddle; Eton mess is an English pudding with strawberries in it.

clue.text: Attractive, thus ultimately cheap?

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word thus

parts.note: crummy means cheap and shoddy

explanation.surface: A question whether something attractive must, in the end, be low quality.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word means delicious or very appealing.

clue.text: Vegetable grass to cover area

indicators.note: cover says the grass and to wrap round the area letter

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grass is grown to cover an area of vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy tuber is one of the most common vegetables.

clue.text: Groom engaged in fighting

parts.note: to comb hair is to groom it
at means engaged in, as in at work

explanation.surface: A bridegroom finds himself caught up in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is armed fighting between forces.

clue.text: Old woman can offer prayer

parts.note: ma is mother, one's old woman informally
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is able to say a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins are morning prayers; the singular form names one such service.

clue.text: My work appears on page …

parts.note: a journalist speaks of the stories they file being printed on a newspaper's pages

explanation.definitionFit: A journalist's stories are printed in the newspaper, so this person's work appears on its pages.

clue.text: In jail I fear this is only nominal?

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words jail I fear

explanation.surface: A prisoner fears that the term of the sentence is in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: A life sentence rarely means imprisonment until death, so the term is only nominal.
explanation.definitionFit: A life term in prison often ends in parole, making the name more nominal than literal.

clue.text: … one badly printed in bold

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: badly says the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing 25, a reporter whose work appears on page one is badly printed in bold type.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 25 across to make one sentence about a newspaper page.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless, daring, bold in spirit.

clue.text: Does it take up space?

parts.note: a cleaning appliance takes up dust, and the word also names a completely empty space

explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum cleaner takes up dirt, while the word itself means empty space with no matter.

clue.text: Criminal's good — strange criminal!

indicators.note: criminal here means wrongly handled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain judged good is a strange villain indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised criminal gang.

clue.text: Assume major is stubborn type

parts.note: to don clothes is to assume them, put them on
a major is a musical key, as in C major

explanation.surface: An officer of major rank presumes to be an obstinate sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is proverbially stubborn, and the word is used for an obstinate person.
